correctness.rationale: For each \(q\ge2\), the exceptional set \(S_q=D_q^{-1}(\operatorname{span}\{D_qB\})\) is a closed proper linear subspace, with properness witnessed by a Fourier mode of frequency different from \(N\). A one-dimensional transverse probe makes each \(S_q\) shy; the standard sigma-ideal property of shy Borel sets makes their countable union shy. Any nontrivial period of a continuous circle function contains a period \(1/q\), and such a period for \(B+\varepsilon\delta\) forces \(\delta\in S_q\). Intersecting this prevalent set with the focal theorem's prevalent acceleration set proves the claim. The quantifiers and small-positive-\(\varepsilon\) range match the source theorem.

value.rationale: The source starts from an exactly \(N\)-fold pullback and uses the resulting translation symmetry in its construction. Showing that every acceleration level \(1,\ldots,N\) still occurs on positive-measure energy sets for a prevalent class whose perturbed potentials have fundamental period exactly one separates the spectral multiplicity phenomenon from any surviving exact covering symmetry. This is a natural structural clarification of what the new theorem is detecting, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or a recomputation.
